questions.question:
**Directions: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.** 

He was not (1)/ grateful for (2)/ Rahul for helping his cause. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '2' i.e. error lies in this part of the sentence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**In this part of the sentence,** the usage of** 'for'** is incorrect Instead, use** 'to'**

 
• **According to grammar**, **'grateful for'** means **'If you are grateful for something that someone has given you or done for you' **and** 'grateful to'** means **'you're grateful to a person.'**
 
• In the given sentence, in part 3 the usage of a proper noun is there hence we need to use 'to' preposition with 'grateful'
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• She was grateful to him for being so good to her.
 
 

**So the correct sentence is- ***He was not **grateful to** Rahul for helping his cause.*

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Erro
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '4' i.e. there is no error in the sentence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's see the formation of the sentence.
 
 
• **'On the one hand'** is a** prepositional phrase** in which *'on' is a preposition and 'the one hand' is a noun phrase*.
 
• **'Life' **is a noun that is the subject of the sentence and '**seems' is a verb that is a verb for this subject.**
 
• **'transient' is an adjective** that is a subject complement of the subject **'life' **because it is connected with the linking verb **'seem' i.e. why it is a subject complement. **
 
• **'and' is coordinate conjunction **and** 'on the other hand'** is a connector here.
 
• **'It' **pronoun is used for** 'life' and again 'is' **is a linking verb *and 'permanent' is an adjective that is used for the subject 'it' and 'with' is a preposition and 'the potential' is a prepositional phrase and 'for' is a preposition 'eternal continuity' is a noun phrase which is a prepositional object of 'for'*
 
 
 
• **Hence, there is no grammatical mistake, the structure is correct.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence ****given**** with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

The big tree was _________ the lake.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Across'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's see the usage of the given prepositions-
 
 
• **In- **is a preposition that means 'expressing the situation of being enclosed or surrounded by something.'

 
 
• Let's see an example
 
• He was in his car.
 
 
 
• **Within- I**s a preposition that means a place, area, or object, it is inside it or surrounded by it.'
 
 
• Let's see an example-
 
• Clients are entertained within private dining rooms.
 
 
 
• **Across-** Is a preposition that means a place or a boundary, they go from one side of it to the other.'
 
 
• Let's see an example-
 
• She walked across the floor and lay down on the bed. 
 
 
 
• **Off- **Is a preposition that means 'something else or moves off it, it is no longer touching that thing.'
 
 
• Let's see an example-
 
• He took his feet off the desk.
 
 
 
 
 
• So according to the meaning of the preposition, the correct answer is **'Across'**

**So the correct sentence is- ***The big tree was **across** the lake.*

**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word. **

Lechery
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Lechery" **refers **to excessive or offensive sexual desire or lustfulness.**
 
• **"Benevolence"** means** kindness, charity, and goodwill, which are positive moral qualities opposed to the negative connotation of "lechery."**
 
• The other options (Lust, Binge, Excess) have meanings that are either similar to or imply some form of indulgence, which aligns more closely with the meaning of "lechery."
 
• The correct** antonym for "lechery" should reflect a concept that is morally good and opposite to lust and indulgence.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

• **Excess** – Inappropriate, suggests overindulgence, aligning more closely with "lechery."

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.** 

I am observing the animals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The animals are being observed'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the Active voice.
 
• Let's see the transformation of the Active voice in the Passive voice.
 
 
• The subject of the sentence in the Active voice becomes the object of the sentence in the passive voice.
 
• The tense of the sentence will remain the same in the passive voice.
 
• If the sentence has an infinitive and doesn't have the object you need to make the passive of the infinitive phrase.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is 'I' and the tense of the sentence is 'present continuous tense' the object of the sentence is 'the animals'
 
• The structure for the present continuous tense is- **be(is/am/are) + Being + V₃**

**So the correct sentence in the passive voice is- ***The animals are being observed. *

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** *

 
• In the given sentence, the 'by me' has not been added because it is optional as 'the verb observe' is both the transitive and intransitive verb hence, in the passive voice its meaning is conveyed that someone has been observing the things. So the given sentence is correct.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.** 

Kavita asked me, “How is your mother?”

options.text: Kavita asked me how was my mother.
Kavita asked her how my mother is.
Kavita asked me how my mother was.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Kavita asked me how my mother was. '**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The given sentence is in 'direct speech' and this is an interrogative sentence.**
 
• Let's see the transformation of the interrogative sentences-
 
 
• *Change in helping verb (Is, are, am, was, who, has, have, had, will, can, could, do, does, did. Interrogative pronoun, adverb, adjective (what, whom, where, why, how, which, what )*
 
• *We can change the verb of reporting speech according to the sense, but shouldn't be changed in the sentence… like we can say we can “asked” “demanded” in the place of “said” and no use of the conjunction “that”.*
 
• *If the sentence starts with an interrogative pronoun or adjective and interrogative adverb, an indirect sentence also starts with these but without conjunction.*
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• She said to me, “how are you?” (Direct speech)
 
• He asked me how I was. (Indirect speech.)
 
 
 
 
 
• *So the correct Indirect speech is written in **option- 4***

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement". **

A case in point is Sydney, Australia, where last year more than 8,000 pedestrians (is fined) for illegally crossing city streets.

• The action occurred "last year," indicating past tense is needed; "were fined" is the correct past plural form of the verb.
